title: Threshold-activated discount review meeting notes
content:
# Threshold-activated discount — notes from the review meeting

Sales / Architecture, 2026-05-06.
Author: Tomek (architecture, taking notes)

Quick draft after today's call with the sales product team. Two parts below — first what they actually want, then what we agreed on the model side. Will turn this into something more formal once Marta signs off.

## What sales is asking for

We have two discount types today:

- the percentage one (e.g. "10% off"), which always applies,
- the value one (e.g. "50 PLN off"), capped at the price so it never goes negative.

Both live in the same place in the model, exposed through a common `Discount` type. Reps don't see the variants — they just hand a `Discount` to whatever calculates the final price.

The complaint from the reps (came up again on Monday): a flat percentage is too blunt. 10% off a 50 PLN accessory is nothing; same 10% off a 600 PLN device is real margin. They want a discount that **only kicks in for prices above some bar** they set. Below the bar — full price, no discount.

So a third kind of discount, with two parameters: percentage + threshold. Threshold is a price (PLN, currency-typed like everywhere else). When applied:

- price above the threshold → reduce by the percentage;
- price at or below the threshold → leave untouched.

Worth listing this out, because the boundary case came up:

- 600 PLN, threshold 500, 10% → 540 PLN (above threshold, applies).
- 500 PLN, threshold 500, 10% → 500 PLN (equal, does NOT apply — strict greater-than, see below).
- 300 PLN, threshold 500, 10% → 300 PLN (below, no change).
- 1000 PLN, threshold 0, 25% → 750 PLN (anything positive clears 0).

Important things they care about:

- It has to plug into the existing `Discount` flow. No second type next to it, no new caller, nothing the rest of the app has to learn. From the outside, `Discount` just has three variants now instead of two.
- They never want a state where the percentage or threshold could be "wrong" (negative, >100%, etc.). If something is malformed, it should fail at the moment we try to construct it, not silently apply a weird discount later.
- The two existing types stay as they are. No renaming, no behaviour change. Their tests must stay green.

Boundary at the threshold: I asked twice. They said the price has to *exceed* the threshold. So strict `>`. Not `>=`. Worth flagging that explicitly because it's the kind of thing that flips during implementation if no one writes it down.

## What we (architecture) agreed on the model side

Sticking close to the existing pattern — that's the easy decision because the two existing discount types are already a clean template.

- New value object next to `PercentageDiscount` and `ValueDiscount`. Same folder, same namespace. Same shape: immutable struct, equality, factory method, no public properties exposing the internals.
- The `Discount` union itself needs touching — it's the type the outside world holds. Today it's two-state with a `bool` discriminator, which obviously won't survive a third variant. We swap the bool for something three-valued (small enum or three flags — Tomasz's preference, doesn't matter much, whatever reads cleanly). Existing factory methods on `Discount` keep their exact signatures so we don't break call sites. Add a third factory for the new variant.
- All validation in the new type's factory. The percentage VO already validates its own range, so we lean on that. The threshold has to be strictly positive — that check is new, lives in the factory, fails fast with a domain error.
- `ApplyOn(Money price)` does the threshold check internally and either applies the percentage or returns the price unchanged. Apply-time code is *not* a place to validate inputs again — by then everything must already be valid.
- Persistence: the SQL repository handles the union as a whole today. Whatever shape it uses, extend the same way for the third variant. Probably no schema change needed, but we'll see when we get there.

Out of scope, just to head off creep:

- No multi-product or cart-level thresholds. Single-product price only.
- No time-bounded promotions.
- No new stacking rules between discount types.
- Not refactoring the existing two types. Not renaming the discriminator field "for clarity" or anything like that. The point is to add a variant, not clean up.

## Open

- Name. I'm calling it `ThresholdDiscount` in my head but I'm not married to it. Anything that mirrors the `...Discount` suffix in the same folder is fine. Will check with Marta.
- Whether to also extend `DiscountsSqlRepository` round-trip tests in this same change or follow up separately — leaning towards same change, otherwise it'll bit-rot.
